meta.purpose: Qwen3-4B attempt terminated at step 0 by the absolute 0.30 collapse early-stop (baseline eval total = 0.255, below threshold). Establishes a third distinct failure mode across the Qwen3 family on this env: 4B emits parseable tool-call JSON on every turn but never commits to a mark_* label action. The agent over-queries until the 50-step env budget exhausts, crashing R4 (step efficiency) to the 0.01 floor. Strictly different from 0.6B's bimodal tool-call emission and 1.7B's entropy collapse.
meta.hardware: Kaggle T4 (8 GB base fit on single cuda:0; device_map='auto' did not pipeline-split despite T4x2 accelerator — 4B fits on one 16 GB T4 with LoRA + 2-gen KV cache)
meta.killed_reason: Absolute 0.30 early-stop fired at step 0 eval (total = 0.255 < 0.30). Known design miss: the early-stop was meant to catch collapse _during_ training; firing on the baseline eval is a false positive. With 3 days to the pitch, not worth re-launching to ~35% chance of a meaningful curve — triple-collapse narrative is stronger evidence than one weak curve.

eval_step_0.note: R4 at the 0.01 floor means ~50 env steps per eval episode (budget exhaustion). Composite: 0.40*0.01 + 0.25*0.01 + 0.25*0.99 + 0.10*0.01 = 0.255. Different signature from 0.6B/1.7B evals which scored 0.353 because R4 hit the ceiling (1 step) — 4B is producing parseable actions on every turn, just not label-committing ones.

summary.entropy: unknown (training never started; can only infer from eval behavior that generation was not degenerate)

Qwen3-0.6B.failure: sometimes clips, sometimes emits — not enough signal to learn chaining

Qwen3-1.7B.failure: deterministic mode collapse; clips at 448 every rollout
Qwen3-1.7B.reward_components_pinned: all components at floor in training rollouts

Qwen3-4B.failure: emits parseable JSON every turn; over-queries until step budget exhausts

summary.finding: The 4-component arithmetic reward surfaces three structurally different failure modes across the Qwen3 family (0.6B, 1.7B, 4B). No model in this range passes the 0.45 red-team ceiling by accident or degeneracy — the env is working as designed, and each reward component (R1 macro-F1, R2 ITC delta, R3 Rule 36(4) compliance, R4 step efficiency) acts as a distinct defense. Training a usable policy requires either (a) tool-SFT warm-start to teach mark_* action preference over query actions before GRPO, (b) a larger-scale model with a better label-vs-query prior in pre-training (Qwen3-8B+, GPT-OSS-20B, Claude), or (c) shaped rewards that dense-encode 'early submit when confident' rather than relying on R4's quadratic penalty kicking in late.
